facts.statement: Macgowania was a small ichthyosaur with a total body length of approximately 3 meters.
facts.quote: It was a small ichthyosaur around 3 m in total body length.

facts.statement: The holotype of Macgowania is a partial skeleton (ROM 41992) that preserves a nearly complete skull, an almost complete forefin, and other postcranial elements.
facts.quote: The first specimen of Macgowania is the holotype ROM 41992 (RBCM EH 91.2.5), a partial skeleton which preserved nearly complete skull, almost complete forefin and other postcranial elements.

facts.statement: Macgowania fossils date to the middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 210 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected in the Jewitt Spur locality from the Pardonet Formation, dating to the middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic, about 210 million years ago.

facts.statement: A second specimen of Macgowania was discovered by a British Columbian outdoor club in August 2009.
facts.quote: A second specimen of Macgowania was discovered by a British Columbian outdoor club in August 2009.

facts.statement: The second specimen was largely complete but was preserved in a fractured rock slab on a steep slope above the Graham River, facing immediate destruction.
facts.quote: This specimen was largely complete, though it was preserved in a fractured slab of rock balanced on a steep slope above the Graham River, in danger of immediate destruction.

facts.statement: Donald Henderson published a scientific description of the second specimen in 2015, identifying it as Macgowania janiceps.
facts.quote: A scientific description of the specimen written by Donald Henderson was published in 2015, in which it was identified as Macgowania janiceps.

facts.statement: The family Macgowaniidae was named by McGowan and Motani in 2003 to include the genus Macgowania.
facts.quote: The family Macgowaniidae was named by McGowan and Motani in 2003 to include this genus.

facts.statement: Macgowania was originally described by Chris McGowan in 1996 under the name Ichthyosaurus janiceps.
facts.quote: Macgowania was originally described by Chris McGowan in 1996 as Ichthyosaurus janiceps.

facts.statement: Ryosuke Motani reassigned the species to its own genus in 1999, establishing Macgowania janiceps as the type species.
facts.quote: It was reassigned to its own genus by Ryosuke Motani in 1999 and the type species is Macgowania janiceps.

facts.statement: The specific name janiceps is derived from Janus, the Roman god with two faces, and ceps, meaning 'with a head'.
facts.quote: The specific name is said to derived from Janus, Latin for the Roman god with two opposite faces, and ceps, Latin for "with a head".

facts.statement: Macgowania belongs to the order Ichthyosauria.
Macgowania is classified within the unranked group Parvipelvia.
The time range for Macgowania is the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
